references.observed: Actually inspected full blue/white main range and chapel corner from above. Continuous long principal range has shallow gray hipped roofs, repeated white chimneys/parapet, raised middle halls and end returns. Five gold onion domes crown the NNE chapel; the tan Lyceum and connecting arch are independent. Detached curved low forecourt ranges are separate native buildings, not roofed over into the palace.

Actually inspected garden side: pale blue plaster, white rusticated lower piers and paired tall white pilasters, two main window stories with small upper attic ovals, gray shallow roofs and white open rooftop balustrade. Gold stucco/cartouche rhythms surround windows; original simplified curved ribbons may suggest these, without copying figures or heraldry. Five gold domes stand at the chapel end.

Actually inspected main forecourt close view: tall arched multi-pane lower and upper windows, small upper attic windows and white pilasters, gold capitals/curved ornament; projecting central entry bay has a real closed pale door and broad supported dark steps. Simpler returned blue side range has three rectangular window stories. Recesses need closed backs and real reveals.

Actually inspected blue chapel/returned range adjacent to tan Lyceum. Gray roof and white parapet/chimneys, gold five-dome cluster behind the corner, white rusticated lower piers and three window rows. Independent tan elevated connecting arch/road passage and Lyceum remain outside the principal-palace model. No copied street signs or text.
